title: Guest-mode messaging, Discord community info, and Live sessions (metadata-only) UI

requirements.summary: Display OmniStream Discord server/community info in an always-visible UI section without adding Discord integration.
acceptanceCriteria: The footer (or another always-visible section) displays Discord server name "ommistream" and contact "scottiscool" in English.
No third-party Discord authentication/integration is added.
If any social icons/links remain that do not have real URLs, they do not misleadingly imply an official Discord link unless a URL is explicitly provided.

file_operations.description: Update the always-visible footer to show Discord community text in English: server "ommistream" and contact "scottiscool". Remove or neutralize any placeholder social links (currently using "#") so they do not imply official links without real URLs.

requirements.summary: Make guest browsing explicit in the UI and clarify that posting/uploading requires sign-in.
acceptanceCriteria: When not signed in, at least one prominent UI location (e.g., NavBar and/or Upload page) shows "Browsing as a guest" (or equivalent) in English.
Upload page unauthenticated state explicitly states that guests can browse but must sign in to upload/post.
Authenticated users do not see guest-only messaging.

file_operations.description: Add a prominent guest-mode indicator in the NavBar when there is no authenticated identity (e.g., "Browsing as a guest"). Ensure it is hidden for authenticated users. Use the existing auth state from the Internet Identity context, aligned with the authorization component’s frontend guidance (guests = anonymous). Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Revise the unauthenticated Upload page state to explicitly message that the user is browsing as a guest and must sign in to upload/post (English). Ensure authenticated users continue to see the upload UI without guest-only messaging.

requirements.summary: Add Live sessions UI: public list + details pages for everyone, and start/end controls for authenticated users (metadata-only).
acceptanceCriteria: A new "Live" (or "Go Live") entry point is available in the app navigation and routes to a dedicated page.
Guests can view a public list of live sessions (including an empty state when none exist).
Authenticated users can start a live session by providing, at minimum, a title; the session becomes visible in the public list as "Live".
Authenticated users can end a live session they started; ended sessions are clearly marked as ended or are removed from the "Live now" list (implementation choice, but must be consistent).

Backend exposes canister methods to create, end, list, and fetch live session metadata, with access control that prevents guests from creating/ending sessions and prevents users from ending sessions they did not start.
This MVP does not require real-time video streaming; it is explicitly metadata/status-driven.

file_operations.description: Add React Query hooks for Live sessions using the existing backend actor capabilities: list active sessions, fetch a session by title, start a session, and end a session. Ensure mutations handle authorization failures gracefully in the UI flow per the authorization component guidance (guests cannot start/end). Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Create a dedicated Live page that (1) shows a public list of active live sessions with an English empty state when none exist, and (2) conditionally shows authenticated-only controls to start a live session (at minimum title; optionally description). Use existing shadcn/ui components already present in the project (e.g., Card/Button) for consistent styling.

Create a Live session details page accessible to all users (including guests) that fetches and displays session metadata (title/description/status/started time). If the viewer is authenticated and is the session owner, show an End Session action; otherwise, do not show end controls. Ensure all user-facing text is English and clearly indicates this is metadata-only (no real streaming).

Register new routes for Live browsing and Live session details (e.g., "/live" and a title-based details route). Wire the routes into the existing TanStack Router route tree so the pages are navigable.
Add a new navigation entry point labeled "Live" (or "Go Live") that routes to the dedicated Live page. Ensure it is visible in the app navigation alongside existing links.
Add a footer Quick Link for the new Live page to keep navigation consistent and ensure the Live area is discoverable.
